svg.title: iPadOS · Interval grading viewer · Crop · landscape
svg.desc: Mirrors the iPad LANDSCAPE editor (a regular-width window wider than tall): App/PhotoViewerView.swift `floatingEditorBody(in:)` — `floatingPictureFrame(in:)` anchors the picture top-left at the size its aspect gives it inside the safe area (a tall picture fills the height, a wide one the width); `touchChrome(showsBadge:)` puts the 36 pt back disc (and, on an interval shoot, the INTERVAL chip — App/EditorControls/EditorMarqueeBadge.swift) top-left and App/EditorControls/EditorTabPill.swift top-right, both 12 pt under the status bar; `floatingFootRow` seats App/EditorControls/EditorGroupBar.swift (`.padPill`, six 58 pt cells) bottom-right and, with a timeline, the compact App/GradeTimelineView.swift strip in a 66 pt capsule bottom-left, both 16 pt off the safe area's foot; `floatingPanel(in:)` floats App/PhotoAdjustmentsPanel.swift (`layout: .floating`, `style: .dark`) as a 400 pt card at right 16 / bottom 96 — above the buttons — draggable by its header (grab bar + title row, `floatingHeaderDragged`, clamped on screen by `clampedFloatingOffset`, the seat kept across groups for the session) and pinned top 62 / bottom 96 when the group is Presets. Pinch, double-tap and trackpad zoom release the picture from its anchor (≤ 1.03× snaps home; a '2.5× · tap to fit' pill then follows the back disc) — desc-only here. iPad PORTRAIT is NOT this layout and not the phone's either: it takes the dark rail (`railBody`, settled 2026-09-13 over spec decision 9), undrawn. Tokens: ground #000, chrome rgba(28,28,30,.85–.86) over .ultraThinMaterial, amber #FFB340 for every highlight, #8E8E93 secondary, diamond #FFB340 with a #C36A00 ring. Geometry measured on an iPad Pro 11-inch (M4) simulator (1210×834 pt) on 2026-09-13 and carried to this 1180×820 canvas: left- and top-anchored positions transfer, trailing ones sit 30 pt further left and foot ones 14 pt higher here; the simulator's safe area is 24 top / 25 bottom, this canvas assumes 24 / 20. THIS FILE is the Crop group: while it is open `floatingPictureFrame` fits the picture inside a margin and CENTRES it instead of anchoring it — 48 pt at the sides, `touchChromeHeight` + 8 = 68 pt at the top and `floatingFootHeight` + 48 = 144 pt at the foot, so a corner handle never lands under the chrome row or the buttons pill — and `openPanel` resets the zoom first. The room is 1084×564 here; this 16:9 picture is height-limited to 1002.7×564 at (88.7, 92) — a 3:4 picture would be 423×564 at (378.5, 92). DEVIATION FROM BOARD 5a, drawn as the app ships it: the board centres with 48 pt on every side (a 1084×724 room); the app keeps the top and foot clear of its own chrome, which on the 2026-09-13 screenshot (screens/ipad-crop.png) measured 96 pt sides / 68 pt above the picture / 144 pt below inside the safe area. App/EditorControls/CropFrameOverlay.swift over the picture with the panel open: a 55 % black scrim outside the crop, a 1 pt white 90 % frame, rule-of-thirds hairlines at white 35 %, and 3 pt white L-brackets with 18 pt arms centred on the corners (36 pt hit areas) — at Original the crop IS the picture, so the frame lies on the picture's edge, the scrim covers nothing and the brackets' outer half is clipped by the pane: they read as a 1.5 pt thickening along 18 pt of each corner, which is what the screenshot shows. Drag the body to move, a corner to resize (locked ratios stay locked), pinch to scale; panel closed with a crop set: an 85 % scrim and the frame alone. The card (same seat, right 16 / bottom 96, 239 pt tall): header 'Crop' with no dot (nothing cropped, no angle); the aspect chips Original · 1:1 · 4:5 · 16:9 · 9:16 · Custom — six equal 57 pt chips 5 apart, 28 pt, radius 12, 11.5 pt semibold, the selected one amber with black text, the rest white 8 % with white text; the hint 'Original · the whole picture' (11 pt, white 50 %; 'Locked to 16:9 · drag to move, pinch or drag a corner to scale' / 'Free crop · drag corners, drag to move, pinch to scale' for the others — the Original wording is the app's, the board says 'Locked to Original · …'); the shared App/RotationSlider.swift (.stacked): 'Angle' 13.5 pt secondary, readout 0° 12.5 pt semibold secondary at neutral, the native Slider tinted amber with its 26 pt white knob centred; and the three-line caption 'Levels the picture and crops in so no corner shows black. Baked into blended and guided clips; set it at more than one moment and it eases between them.' at 11 pt tertiary. Buttons pill: Crop open. Staged by LL_EDITOR=latest LL_VIEWER=1 LL_KEYFRAMES=sunset LL_SECTIONS=crop on an iPad Pro 11-inch simulator (the interval project, so the strip and INTERVAL chip are drawn too).
